$description:
vcskill design tokens. Authored in DTCG with OKLCH colour. This file is the single source; packages/tokens/dist/*.css is generated and must never be hand-edited.

Design thesis — execution cartography for agent engineers: ink-black ground, spectral blue for live execution, copper for human gates, cool-white for surfaces, graphite for structure. The visual language is topology, gates, checkpoints, and path witnesses.

ink.$description: The ground. Everything is drawn on ink, never on pure black.

spectral.$description: Live execution: an active path, a running node, a resolved witness.

copper.$description: Human gates: approval required, held, awaiting a decision.

signal.$description: Outcome states. Deliberately narrow: cartography carries meaning, colour only confirms it.

surface.$description: Semantic surface roles. Apps consume these, never a raw palette step.

text.$description: Text roles on the canvas. Contrast against surface.canvas is asserted by tests/tokens/token-contract.test.mjs.

topology.$description: The execution graph itself. A path witness is the record that a given edge was actually taken.

state.$description: Interactive state layers. NOT every state gets a unique colour — the token set carries meaning in layer + border + text + indicator roles so shape and text can share the burden with colour. Apps consume state.* aliases; screens never restate a raw palette step for a state.

hover.$description: A subtle raise, not a highlight. The layer sits ON TOP of surface.canvas / surface.raised.

pressed.$description: A deeper depression than hover; readers should feel one click of extra weight.

selected.$description: A held selection (e.g. a chosen row, a picked filter). Selection is a DIFFERENT state from current — current is the reader's own position; selected is a chosen value.

current.$description: The reader's own position in navigation, breadcrumb, sibling list, or TOC. Carried as a left/inline indicator bar; NEVER a fill, so nav-current does not collide visually with selection.

disabled.$description: Non-interactive. Contrast intentionally drops; disabled elements are not required to meet 4.5:1 on text, per WCAG 2.2 disabled-control exemption. Still visible enough to read.

loading.$description: In-flight work: a spinner, a determinate/indeterminate progress bar. Loading uses spectral to match live-execution semantics.

success.$description: An outcome-confirmed state. Distinct from copy-success (which is a transient toast) — success here marks the persistent status of a completed operation.

error.$description: A failed operation. Distinct from destructive — destructive is a boundary before action; error is a resulting state.

destructive.$description: A boundary marker for an irreversible action (rm, drop, force-push, delete). MUST render before the action fires, not after. Uses signal.fail hue for hazard recognition.

copySuccess.$description: The transient copy-to-clipboard witness. Distinct from execution witness so the visual meanings don't collide — copySuccess is 'we did the local UI thing', witness is 'the remote/server thing was recorded'.

content.$description: Content-surface roles for code, data, callouts, and empty/error states. These wrap surface aliases with content-specific semantics so a screen author writes `content.code.background`, not `color.ink.700`.

code.$description: Fenced code / command surface. Uses ink.800 (one step raised from canvas) so it reads as a distinct region on both surface.canvas and surface.raised parents.

codeInline.$description: Inline `code` chip. Slightly smaller inset than a fenced block.

table.$description: Data table surfaces. Rows do NOT alternate by default; a stripe is available for very-long tables when the eye needs a rest line.

callout.$description: Five named callouts. Each carries a distinct semantic — do not add a sixth without an accepted decision-doc addendum.

overlay.$description: Modal, drawer, and popover surfaces. Overlay uses ink.700 so it reads above the canvas without a glow.

selection.$description: Text-selection background (the browser default is usually opinionated; we override it once, here).

empty.$description: Empty-state surface (no rows, no results, no matches).

errorSurface.$description: Non-inline error surface (e.g. a failed panel). Distinct name from state.error so a screen can compose both — one is the visual container, the other is the state alias applied to controls inside it.

weight.$description: Inter body is a variable face pinned 400..700 in the manifest; `medium` (500) is a legitimate axis position, not a fake alias. The display face (Be Vietnam Pro) is a single 700 asset — do NOT add a display-medium role; use text-size, spacing, and color for hierarchy instead.

size.$description: A fifth-major scale. Body is 1rem; nothing below 0.875rem is used for prose.

space.$description: A strict 4px base grid. Every spacing value is a multiple of 0.25rem.

size.$description: Interaction sizing. touchTarget is the WCAG 2.2 target-size floor and is asserted by tests.

layout.$description: Shared shell/composition dimensions. Values on the 4px grid or documented if not. Marked shared vs app-local in docs/decisions/state-layers-content-surfaces-and-dimensions.md.

docs.$description: The docs shell composition. Shared across both apps' documentation rendering.

table.$description: Data-table column constraints. Rows never scroll horizontally on the page; the table itself carries a local scroll affordance.

marketing.$description: Marketing surface composition gaps for split/path/ledger sections. app-local: only the site consumes these; docs never composes marketing gaps.

density.$description: Row / list densities. Compact for tight reference; prose for reading; reference for the CLI options tables. All ≥ touchTarget where the row is interactive.

radius.$description: Geometric, not soft. The largest radius is deliberately small; cartography reads as drafted, not rounded.

focus.$description: A single focus treatment across both apps. The ring must never be removed, only re-coloured on a light surface.

duration.$description: Short by design. Anything above 400ms reads as latency rather than feedback.

elevation.$description: Elevation is drawn with a hairline and a soft ground shadow, never with a glow.
